This is the PRECISION half of M4-01's acceptance criterion, which
docs/PLAN-M4.md states and the M4 round never ran. The audit is
docs/QA-EPG-PRECISION.md.
RE-LEVELLED 2026-10-04 BY F-EPG-11, AND THE ORACLE COLLAPSED WITH IT.
`oracle` entries were graded by an identifier the matcher did not read:
the Pluto channel id in each row's own stream URL. F-EPG-11 makes the
matcher read exactly that identifier, so 8 of this fixture's 9 pairs are
now matched BY the thing that used to grade them and `oracle` is a
tautology, not evidence. It is kept because it still pins the wiring, and
`oracleIsNowTheMatcher` makes the collapse an assertion rather than a
footnote. The one pair still graded by something the matcher never read is
in `returnedByRepair`, matched by NAME.
A grader that does not depend on the stream URL is owed to this fixture;
until one exists the precision question is OPEN, not answered here.
channelTotal 11 = 5 address pairs + 1 D-EPG-5 row + 2 country-qualifier
rows (F-EPG-7, now matched by address) + 2 News12 rows + 1 Tennis row
(F-EPG-8, now matched by address).
matched 9 = the 5 address pairs, the 2 country-qualifier rows, the Tennis
row, and News12 Long Island by name.
warnings: 1 programmes for channels not in the playlist dropped

why: REPAIRED 2026-10-03. epg_name_key folds on normalize_id_text, which keeps the +.
Kept as the record of the defect and of what the repair cost and returned:
on this fixture the wrong Bloomberg pair goes and News12 Long Island arrives,
so matched stays 6 and nameDroppedPlaylist falls from 2 to 0. On the real
1,453-channel list the same change reads matched 227 -> 226, nameIndexed
1,443 -> 1,453 and nameDroppedPlaylist 10 -> 0.

unmatched.why: REPAIRED: the id fold keeps the + that separates Bloomberg TV from the guide's Bloomberg TV+, so this pair no longer forms. This row streams from an unbranded address and so is out of F-EPG-11's reach too, which is why it is the one row here that still tests the NAME rule's precision

note: Both names run through epg_name_key and normalize_id_text in the test:
the first makes them equal, the second does not. The second name is
the guide's declaration, not a playlist row.

returnedByRepair.why: The row the + fold used to deny. It carries no Pluto id, so the oracle cannot confirm it the way it confirms the five above; it is right by reading, and it is here rather than in `oracle` so the two kinds of evidence stay distinguishable.

why: Every plutoId below is now a key of build_alias's `addr` map pointing at
that same tvgId, which is precisely what the matcher looks a guide
channel up by. The test asserts that, so the collapse cannot be
forgotten: if the two ever become independent again this fixture says so
by going red.
The name key still keeps '(United States)' and still cannot match: that
half of F-EPG-7 is unchanged and asserted. What changed is that the
pair no longer costs anything, because the address reaches it.
Measured on the frozen inputs: the parenthetical strip was worth 29
rows and one CONTRADICTED pair before F-EPG-11 and is worth 1 row and
zero contradicted pairs after it.
the second country-qualifier row, same rule
